newsitem.title: GERMANY: Trinkaus cuts BMW, raises VW.
newsitem.headline: Trinkaus cuts BMW, raises VW.

text.p: Trinkaus Capital Management said on Thursday it had lowered its rating for BMW AG shares to neutral from overweight.
Trinkaus also said it had raised its recommendation for VW shares to overweight from neutral.
Trinkaus said in a statement it was maintaining its positive assessment of BMW and its shares in the medium term and long term.
But it added that the strong appreciation of the British pound was likely to mean that earnings gains at BMW's UK subsidiary Rover in 1996 and 1997 would be lower than it had expected.
Trinkaus predicted BMW shares would show a below-average performance over the next three months in comparison with other car stocks.
While other manufacturers will benefit from positive media coverage due to new models, the new BMW 3 Series will only come into play later this year, Trinkaus said.
"From a trading point of view we therefore recommend reducing the overweighting of BMW and in turn take a stronger position in VW shares," Trinkaus said.
Trinkaus said the settlement of VW's industrial espionage dispute with General Motors had averted the threat of compensation payments that could have endangered the entire VW group.
The compensation payment of $100 million by VW to GM would scarcely have any effect on earnings and the VW shares were likely to outperform over the next three months.
Only the interim report for the first quarter of 1997, due in April, harboured the danger that analysts' upbeat expectations for VW might be disappointed, Trinkaus said.
